en.name: Pastrami
en.summary: Pastrami is beef — usually navel or brisket — cured in brine, rubbed with coriander and pepper, smoked and then steamed. Sold sealed and refrigerated, it keeps about 40 days at 4 °C (40 °F) or below. Once the pack is open that no longer applies and it becomes an ordinary opened deli meat.
en.pantry: Pastrami is a refrigerated product and belongs in the cold from the counter to the plate. The cure and the smoke extend its fridge life but do not make it shelf-stable — it is a moist, ready-to-eat meat, which is the category that most rewards careful temperature control. Out of the fridge, the two-hour rule applies, or one hour above 32 °C (90 °F); a sandwich left in a warm car is the classic way people get this wrong.
en.fridge: Keep a sealed commercial pack at 4 °C (40 °F) or below and it runs about 40 days, or to the printed date if that falls sooner. That figure is for the intact pack: once you open it, or once it has been sliced for you at a deli counter, you have an opened ready-to-eat meat and should eat it within a few days rather than counting on the rest of the forty. Re-wrap opened slices tightly, keep them at the back of the fridge rather than in the door, and keep them away from raw meat.
en.freezer: No freezer timeline is given for pastrami here, so this page will not invent one. Freezing it is possible and it will be safe indefinitely at −18 °C (0 °F), but a brined, steamed meat gives up a lot in the freezer: the slices weep on thawing and the texture goes spongy. If you have more than you can eat, it is better used up in hash, sandwiches and soups than put away for later.
en.thawing: If you have frozen it anyway, thaw it in the fridge, still wrapped, and use it within a couple of days. Never on the counter.
spoilage: Slime or a sticky film on the slices — the usual first sign on a ready-to-eat meat.
A sour or yeasty smell instead of a peppery, smoky one.
Grey-green or iridescent patches on the cut surfaces.
A pack that has gone puffy or is leaking before it is opened.
tips: Buy it sliced only when you will eat it within a few days; buy the piece if you want the long fridge life.
Write the opening date on the pack — forty days and a few days are not the same number.
Store it on a shelf, not the door, where the temperature swings least.
Steam or microwave slices briefly rather than eating them fridge-cold; hot pastrami is also the safer habit.

faq.q: How long does pastrami keep in the fridge?
faq.a: About 40 days for a sealed commercial pack at 4 °C (40 °F) or below, or the printed date if that is sooner. Opened, only a few days.
There is no timeline for it here. It will be safe at −18 °C, but brined, steamed beef thaws watery and spongy, so it is better eaten fresh.

faq.q: Does pastrami need to be refrigerated?
faq.a: Yes. Curing and smoking lengthen its fridge life but do not make it shelf-stable.

zh.name: 煙燻醃牛肉
zh.summary: Pastrami 是牛肉（通常是腹脅或前胸肉）先泡鹽水醃漬，抹上香菜籽與粗黑胡椒後煙燻，再蒸熟。以密封冷藏品販售時，在 4 °C 以下大約可放 40 天。包裝一旦打開，這個數字就不再適用，它就變成一般的「已開封即食冷肉」。
zh.pantry: Pastrami 是冷藏品，從櫃檯到餐盤都該待在低溫。醃漬和煙燻延長了它的冷藏壽命，但沒有讓它變成常溫品——它是一種濕潤的即食肉，而這一類正是最需要溫度管理的食品。離開冰箱後適用 2 小時原則，室溫超過 32 °C 時為 1 小時；把三明治留在悶熱的車上，就是最常見的出錯方式。
zh.fridge: 未開封的市售密封包裝放 4 °C 以下，大約 40 天，若標示日期更早則以標示為準。這個數字只適用於完整未破的包裝：一旦拆封，或請熟食櫃現切，你手上的就是已開封的即食肉品，應該在幾天內吃完，而不是繼續數那四十天。開封後的切片要重新包緊，放冰箱內側深處而不是門邊，並和生肉分開。
zh.freezer: 這裡沒有給 pastrami 的冷凍期限，本頁也不會憑空生一個。冷凍當然可行，在 −18 °C 下安全性是無限期的，但鹽漬又蒸過的肉在冷凍庫裡損失很大：解凍時會出水，口感變得像海綿。吃不完的話，做成薯泥煎肉餅、三明治或湯用掉，比冰起來留著好。
zh.thawing: 如果還是冷凍了，請維持包裝放冷藏解凍，兩三天內用完。不要放室溫。
spoilage: 切片發黏、表面有黏膜——即食肉品最典型的第一個訊號。
聞起來發酸或有酵母味，而不是胡椒與煙燻香。
切面出現灰綠色或虹彩般的斑塊。
還沒開封就已經脹袋或滲液。
tips: 幾天內吃得完再買切片；想要長一點的冷藏壽命就買整塊。
在包裝上寫開封日——四十天和幾天完全是兩回事。
放層架不要放冰箱門，那裡溫度起伏最小。
切片稍微蒸一下或微波再吃，不要冰冷直接吃；加熱過也比較保險。

faq.q: 煙燻醃牛肉冷藏可以放多久？
faq.a: 未開封的市售密封包在 4 °C 以下約 40 天，若包裝日期更早則以包裝為準。開封後只有幾天。

faq.q: 煙燻醃牛肉可以冷凍嗎？
faq.a: 這裡沒有對應期限。−18 °C 下安全沒問題，但鹽漬蒸製的牛肉解凍後會出水、口感變海綿，建議趁新鮮吃完。

faq.q: 煙燻醃牛肉需要冷藏嗎？
faq.a: 需要。醃漬和煙燻只是延長冷藏壽命，並沒有讓它變成常溫品。
